task.title: Move canonical project identity into a refs/workbook/project ref
task.description:
Project identity currently lives in branch content (.workbook/config.json), which is why a checkout cut before Workbook adoption looks like a new project (see "workbook: tracked Workbook configuration does not match common project guard"). Reverse the roles: an immutable identity record moves into a tool-private ref, and the committed file keeps only human-visible, mutable project preferences.

## Design

- Publish a refs/workbook/project ref holding the canonical identity document: format, projectId, and key (the key is baked into every task ID ever minted, so it rides with identity, not preferences). Identity is immutable after mint; publication uses compare-and-swap locally and non-fast-forward rejection remotely, matching the task refs. The ref must live outside refs/workbook/tasks/* so v0.4.x clients, whose fetch refspecs and ls-remote patterns name only the task namespace, never see it.
- .workbook/config.json becomes the mutable preferences document (autoSync today; the planned status-column work lands under this paradigm). It no longer carries authoritative identity: drop projectId from the document, or keep it strictly advisory and opportunistically rewritten. Human visibility of the ID is already served by the generated .workbook/guidelines.md.
- Bootstrap precedence in setup/sync: identity ref exists (locally or on origin) -> it wins; no ref but the tracked file carries identity -> adopt the file's identity and publish the ref once (self-healing migration for existing projects); neither -> mint and publish. Setup on any branch then works with no tracked file at all, which makes the pre-Workbook-branch bug structurally impossible rather than merely handled.
- The private guard at .git/workbook/project.json collapses: refs already live in the common Git directory shared by every worktree, so the local identity ref is the per-repo record the guard was approximating. The SQLite projection keeps validating its stored project_id.
- Fork semantics change deliberately: forks copy branches but not refs/workbook/*, so setup in a fork mints a fresh, empty project instead of silently inheriting the upstream identity; document an explicit ref push (git push fork 'refs/workbook/*:refs/workbook/*') as the way to carry a tracker over.

## Migration (required, must be a clean path)

A mixed-version team must keep working: one teammate upgrading to v0.5.0 and publishing the identity ref must not break a teammate still on v0.4.x.

- v0.4.x clients ignore the new ref (their refspecs never fetch it), so publishing it is invisible to them.
- v0.5.0 must keep the committed file's identity fields intact and readable by v0.4.x during a deprecation window: adopt-and-publish must not rewrite or strip the tracked file as a side effect. Removing identity from the tracked document is a deliberate, opt-in upgrade (the existing UpgradeConfig discipline: a change that makes the project unreadable to older binaries belongs to a command the user ran on purpose, not to every mutation).
- While both sources exist they must agree; v0.5.0 treats the ref as canonical and reports (not wedges on) a stale file.
- Spell out the rollout in README: upgrade order does not matter, nothing breaks until the project deliberately upgrades its tracked document version, and by then every clone should be on v0.5.0.

---

**Design resolution (2026-08-11, supersedes the paragraphs above where they differ):**
- Mutable project configuration (the status vocabulary, and future config families) lives in a SEPARATE synced operation-ledger ref, refs/workbook/config, owned by WB-01KYQPKSGAMTB9TQZEV17RGY55 -- not in .workbook/config.json. The tracked file keeps autoSync as a real input and its identity fields as ADVISORY copies; slimming the file (v3) is deferred beyond v0.5.0.
- The committed human-visible rendering of the vocabulary is the generated guidelines.md table only; .workbook/config.json gains no vocabulary block (ProjectConfig must remain comparable -- Go struct equality is load-bearing).
- The private guard at .git/workbook/project.json is still WRITTEN in v0.5.0 and auto-REPAIRED from the ref when it disagrees (the old wedge becomes self-healing); deleting it is v0.6.x work.
- Identity-field disagreement between ref and file is FATAL with a message naming every source and the remedy; "report, not wedge" applies to document-version drift, not identity.
- The identity commit is deterministic (fixed author/committer/date/message) so concurrent adopters of the same identity converge to the same object ID and the second publish is a no-op.
